links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM diagnoses across repeated runs on different days
links.effect: GPT 3.5 on 927 texts over 3 days: 6 cases (0.65%) had different diagnoses, 70% textual variation; rerun of all configurations averaged 1.7 changes in confusion matrices.
links.quote: Diagnoses: Most notably, 6 cases (0.65%) presented different diagnoses on at least 2 different days.

links.outcome: Comparison of candidate GPT model configurations against expert physician labels on same data
links.effect: GPT 4 Turbo precision 90.6%, sensitivity 100%, kappa 0.95; GPT 3.5 precision 44.9%, kappa 0.59; GPT 3.5+4 precision 81.0%, kappa 0.88.
links.quote: The best results came using configuration 3, the GPT 4 Turbo.

links.outcome: Reference standard by expert physicians labeling texts for anaphylaxis
links.effect: Three expert physicians reviewed and classified all texts before experiments; no blinding or adjudication procedure or inter-rater agreement is reported.
links.quote: The 3 specialists reviewed all texts and classified all cases as anaphylaxis or not before these experiments.

links.outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy against expert ground-truth labels
links.effect: GPT 4 Turbo: 90.6% precision, 100% sensitivity, 99.5% specificity, 99.5% accuracy, kappa 0.95.
links.quote: The best results came using configuration 3, the GPT 4 Turbo.

links.outcome: Effect of adding WAO criteria to prompt on LLM precision
links.effect: WAO criteria improved GPT 3.5 precision from 44.9% to 60.8% and GPT 3.5+4 from 81.0% to 84.2%; GPT 4 Turbo precision did not improve (90.6% to 88.9%).
links.quote: It reached the point that GPT 4 Turbo precision did not improve with the additional information.

links.outcome: Anaphylaxis classification accuracy against physician labels
links.effect: Best model: TP 48, FP 5, TN 916, FN 0; precision 90.6%, sensitivity 100%, specificity 99.5%, accuracy 99.5%.
links.quote: Using the primary prompt, GPT 4 Turbo detected anaphylaxis cases with 90.6% precision, 100% sensitivity, 99.5% specificity, 99.5% accuracy, and a Cohen kappa coefficient of 0.95.

links.effect: Initial GPT 3.5 consistency test: 6/927 (0.65%) different diagnoses; later reruns changed 0-3 cases/configuration, average 1.7.
links.quote: Most notably, 6 cases (0.65%) presented different diagnoses on at least 2 different days.

links.outcome: Performance after removing easy negative texts
links.effect: Without SemClinBR, GPT4 Turbo specificity 99.5%→90.2%, accuracy 99.5%→95%, kappa 0.95→0.90; precision/sensitivity unchanged.
links.quote: Specificity went from 99.5% to 90.2%, and accuracy from 99.5% to 95%, still outstanding results.

links.effect: GPT 4 Turbo was best: precision 90.6%, kappa 0.95; WAO improved GPT3.5 precision 44.9%→60.8% and GPT3.5+4 81.0%→84.2%.
links.quote: The WAO criteria did improve the older models’ performance, as for GPT 3.5 + 4 configuration, precision went from 81.0% to 84.2% and kappa from 0.88 to 0.9, and for the GPT 3.5, configuration had even more improvements, with precision going from 44.9% to 60.8% and kappa from 0.59 to 0.74.
